_leia: Gerado pelo build a partir dos campos `en` de conteudo/catalogo.json e conteudo/fichas.json. Sobreposto ao português por src/scripts/conteudo.js, campo a campo: o que falta aqui aparece em português na versão inglesa.

linhasAcao.1.1: 1.1. Strengthen the rollout of ecological-economic zoning (ZEE) and of the protected-area system, and the land-use planning that follows from them.
linhasAcao.1.2: 1.2. Ensure that climate adaptation plans exist and are running in every state of the Legal Amazon.
linhasAcao.1.3: 1.3. Prevent, fight, control and monitor illegal forest fires, illegal clearing and environmental crime.
linhasAcao.1.4: 1.4. Recover degraded land across the Legal Amazon, with an emphasis on ecological and productive restoration.
linhasAcao.1.5: 1.5. Build a multi-level land and environmental governance system, using remote sensing and interoperable registries.
linhasAcao.2.1: 2.1. Eradicate extreme poverty and reduce poverty in the Legal Amazon, advancing social inclusion and income generation.
linhasAcao.2.2: 2.2. Strengthen management and widen the reach and quality of public health services, with an emphasis on reducing avoidable deaths.
linhasAcao.2.3: 2.3. Strengthen public education in the Legal Amazon, with an emphasis on raising the quality indicators of basic education.
linhasAcao.2.4: 2.4. Improve public safety in the region, with an emphasis on reducing intentional violent deaths and on protecting communities.
linhasAcao.2.5: 2.5. Create jobs and income by building an inclusive, modern business environment.
linhasAcao.3.1: 3.1. Raise the share of the socio-bioeconomy in regional GDP by strengthening its value chains.
linhasAcao.3.2: 3.2. Widen the supply of green jobs through the transition to a low-carbon economy and the valuing of standing forest.
linhasAcao.3.3: 3.3. Promote technical and vocational training in the socio-bioeconomy through capacity-building initiatives.
linhasAcao.3.4: 3.4. Increase the number of beneficiaries and the range of payment-for-ecosystem-services instruments, focusing on traditional populations.
linhasAcao.3.5: 3.5. Establish intelligent, orderly use of mineral resources, including adding value to the minerals extracted.
linhasAcao.4.1: 4.1. Expand and integrate technological infrastructure in the Legal Amazon, advancing universal digital connectivity.
linhasAcao.4.2: 4.2. Expand, modernise and integrate the intermodal transport and logistics network across the region and the Pan-Amazon.
linhasAcao.4.3: 4.3. Drive the energy transition in the Legal Amazon, with an emphasis on generating and distributing more renewable power.
linhasAcao.4.4: 4.4. Put in place urban development and integrated sanitation policies with modern, resilient infrastructure.
linhasAcao.5.1: 5.1. Raise more finance through national and international partnerships for sustainable development.
linhasAcao.5.2: 5.2. Strengthen governance, cooperation and multi-level integration between states, across borders and with the private sector.
linhasAcao.5.3: 5.3. Build the capacity to put in place a fair climate legal framework for the Legal Amazon, and cooperate around it.
linhasAcao.5.4: 5.4. Expand and strengthen research, development and innovation in the Legal Amazon, with incentives to match.
linhasAcao.5.5: 5.5. Strengthen the governance and management of public services in the Legal Amazon, with an emphasis on the sound use of public resources.

I1.1.2: Ncompliant = state protected areas meeting both management criteria: yes to a management plan and yes to a governing council.
Ntotal = all state protected areas on the official register (CNUC/MMA).
I1.3.2: Dillegal = area cleared without a permit, in hectares.
Dtotal = total area cleared in the year, as measured by PRODES/INPE.
Apermitted = area with a clearing permit issued through Sinaflor/IBAMA.
I1.3.4: FAL = total fire hotspots in the Legal Amazon in the year.
Fu = hotspots detected in state u by the reference satellite of INPE’s Queimadas programme.
u = each of the nine states of the region.
I2.1.1: Npeople in poverty = population living in poverty in the reference year (IBGE/SIS).
Ppopulation that year = total population of the same unit, in the same year.
I2.2.2: nFHT = Family Health Teams in the state, at a parameter of 3,500 people per team.
nPCT20 and nPCT30 = 20-hour and 30-hour Primary Care Teams, at parameters of 1,750 and 2,625 people.
Pspecial teams = population registered with street clinic, riverside and river-boat teams, as reported in Sisab.
PIBGE = IBGE population estimate for the state’s municipalities taken together.
I2.2.3: Mwith active service = municipalities with a telehealth facility active in the CNES register.
Mtotal in the Legal Amazon = the 808 municipalities of the Legal Amazon.
I2.3.1: Mthat met the target = municipalities that met or beat the IDEB target projected by INEP.
Mtotal = municipalities with a published IDEB score for the stage assessed — primary, lower secondary or upper secondary.
I2.3.2: Nenrolled = basic education enrolments recorded in INEP’s school census.
P4–17 = IBGE population projection for the 4-to-17 age band.
I2.4.1: VCVLI = victims of intentional violent deaths recorded by Sinesp/Ministry of Justice.
President = resident population estimated by IBGE for the same year.
I3.4.1: Rtotal = funds committed to payment-for-ecosystem-services programmes, in reais.
Nbeneficiaries = people or families reached by those programmes in the same period.
I3.4.2: Rspent = funds actually paid out in the financial year.
Rbudgeted = funds authorised in the budget for the same year.
I4.3.2: The published figure uses the licensed capacity of plants in operation (SIGA/ANEEL) as a proxy for energy supply — which is why it sits above the official baseline of 65.24%.
I4.4.1: HH = households; m = each municipality of the Legal Amazon; R = the region as a whole.
The hydrological factor is not published by IBGE and was assumed to be 1 during collection, which raises the result against the official baseline of 41.52%.
I5.2.1: Rprivate mobilised = private capital drawn in by the regional blended finance mechanisms.
Rpublic committed = public funds put into those same mechanisms.
The ratio says how many reais of private money each real of public money brings in.
I5.2.2: Linear projection based on the Consortium’s budget execution between 2019 and 2026.
I5.5.1: The final CAPAG rating combines the three financial dimensions the National Treasury assesses.
